answer: Each lobster pot carries a buoy painted with its owner's mark, and the registry holds the mark of every pot in the bay. A dune pot hauled on a day it was never set fails the registry: at the grove of the buoy the paint must match the registry's own mark, and a strange buoy floats on another man's rope. Faking a fleet means buying fifty pots, painting false marks and paying 13,500, and the glacier entry in the registry is read at every hauling, so a pot whose mark belongs to no fisherman is cut loose.
